govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AssassinationJF: This correspondence on the JFK autopsy photographs and X-rays — creator unknown — is a file on the disputed evidence. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The autopsy materials remain controversial. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BantaCo_Banta_C: This George Banta Company printing quotation — July 21, 1975 — is a printer’s price note. The file belongs to the business archive. Banta printed books and magazines for decades. Researchers value such files. The item is a fragment of trade history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAMexico_CIA_M: Philip Agee’s memorandum on Mexico City CIA officers — January 15, 1967 — comes from the ex-agent’s Inside the Company. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. Agee’s 1975 exposé named names. The item is a fragment of the exposé.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Counter-revolut: Fenton Wheeler’s Castro Death Plot Revealed covers a plot against Castro. The CIA plotted against Castro for years. The plots all failed. The story caused a stir. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DallasCountyJai: Harold Weisberg’s memo — 17 Dallas County Jail Prisoners Not Interviewed by FBI — is a researcher’s note. The file belongs to the assassination archive. Weisberg tracked the investigation’s gaps. The gaps troubled him. The item is a fragment of the record.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-de-maris: A 1913 entry on Adam de Marisco — Adam Marsh, the Franciscan friend of Grosseteste. Francis Urquhart tells his learned life. Oxford's first Franciscan doctor. A friar among England's great minds. His letters to Grosseteste survive. The friars loved him as a father.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agostino-steu: This 1913 reference article on Agostino Steuco — the Augustinian scholar of the perennial philosophy. Michael Ott praises his De perenni philosophia. He found one truth in many sages. The Vatican library housed his labors. A humanist in a friar's habit. His pages charmed the Renaissance popes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-amico: A 1913 entry on Antonio Amico — a Sicilian churchman of note. Thomas Shahan records his career. The entry preserves his modest fame. His pen served the Palermo church. A canon among the writers. His chronicle served the Sicilian scholars. His see was the island's primacy.
